tour.title: Mold at a Glance
tour.description: Begin with the root README to learn what Mold generates, which model families it supports, and how its local-first CLI relates to the server and graphical clients. This overview supplies the vocabulary and system boundaries used throughout the rest of the tour.

tour.title: Workspace Shape
tour.description: The root Cargo manifest defines the Rust workspace that underpins Mold's core platform. Read it after the README to see how the CLI, shared contracts, persistence, inference, and server are assembled as separately testable crates with feature-gated build behavior.
tour.languageLesson: Cargo workspaces coordinate versions, dependencies, and feature flags across multiple Rust crates while preserving crate-level compilation boundaries.

tour.title: CLI Bootstrap
tour.description: The CLI main module is the primary code entry point identified by the graph, and it loads configuration before dispatching into the command tree. Follow the generate and serve commands to see the two defining modes introduced in the README: execute generation locally or expose the same capabilities through a server.
tour.languageLesson: Rust command-line applications commonly use enums for subcommand dispatch and modules to keep each command's parsing and execution path isolated.

tour.title: Core Contracts
tour.description: Beneath the CLI, mold-core establishes the shared types, configuration rules, paths, and public interfaces used across runtime boundaries. Its types module has the graph's highest fan-out, making these contracts the central vocabulary that keeps the CLI, server, and clients aligned.
tour.languageLesson: Rust library crates expose a deliberate public API through lib.rs; shared structs and enums can then serve as compile-time contracts between otherwise independent crates.

tour.title: Inference Engine
tour.description: Building on the core request types, mold-inference defines the common engine contract for loading models and executing generation. The factory maps model families and enabled features to concrete engines, allowing many image and video pipelines to sit behind one runtime-facing abstraction.
tour.languageLesson: Rust traits provide a shared behavioral interface, while feature-gated factory construction keeps optional model backends out of builds that do not need them.

tour.title: Durable Runtime State
tour.description: Generation is more than an in-memory inference call, so mold-db persists application state and evolves it through migrations. The generation queue is the bridge between accepted work and later execution, giving server and client workflows durable scheduling state rather than tying them to one process interaction.

tour.title: Authenticated Server API
tour.description: The Axum server composes the core contracts, inference runtime, and persisted queue into the HTTP service used by remote clients. Routes define the authenticated API surface, while shared state coordinates the long-lived services and runtime data that handlers need.
tour.languageLesson: Axum applications build a router from typed handlers and inject shared state into asynchronous requests, keeping transport concerns separate from underlying domain services.

tour.title: Shared Studio Logic
tour.description: With the wire service established, the Studio package provides reusable client contracts and workflows for every Vue surface. Its API client speaks to the server, while host routing chooses capable machines and preserves frozen-route semantics so a generation remains bound to the machine that accepted it.
tour.languageLesson: A shared TypeScript package lets multiple frontends reuse pure policies and wire contracts without coupling their platform-specific stores or native bridges.

tour.title: Web Client
tour.description: The web entry point mounts Mold Studio in the browser on top of the shared logic from the previous step. Its authenticated HTTP and SSE API module carries requests and live events, while the web types keep the surface aligned with wire-level data contracts.

tour.title: Desktop Application
tour.description: The desktop TypeScript entry mounts the Vue application, whose root coordinates routing, host connectivity, notifications, and global overlays. The router organizes the desktop workspaces, while the Tauri configuration describes how this web UI is packaged with its native desktop shell.
tour.languageLesson: Tauri pairs a web frontend with a native Rust host, using configuration to define the packaged application and an explicit bridge for privileged platform operations.

tour.title: Remote Mobile Client
tour.description: Mobile reuses the Studio policies and a dedicated Vue entry, with MobileApp orchestrating the remote-only workspace experience instead of embedding a local inference engine. The thin Tauri native shell adds secure credentials, discovery, media, appearance, and background-task services, and its configuration supplies the mobile package contract.

tour.title: Container Packaging
tour.description: The Dockerfile turns the Rust platform and web assets into deployable artifacts after the application layers are understood. Separate web-builder, Rust builder, and CUDA stages make the packaging flow explicit and let heavyweight GPU runtime concerns remain isolated from frontend compilation.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds separate compilation environments from final runtime images, improving cache reuse and avoiding unnecessary build dependencies in shipped artifacts.

tour.title: Validation and Releases
tour.description: Finish with the automation that protects and publishes the architecture visited in earlier steps. The core CI workflow validates the Rust and shared project contracts, target workflows cover desktop, iOS, and Android surfaces, and the release workflow packages the resulting artifacts for distribution.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use event triggers, parallel jobs, and ordered steps; target-specific pipelines keep platform contracts visible while a release pipeline coordinates publication.
